title: From the SEM to the TEO-5
intro: The TEO-5 is Oberheim’s compact five-voice polysynth, released in 2024 and made with Sequential on the platform of the Take 5. Where the Take 5 has a low-pass filter, the TEO-5 has a 12 dB state-variable filter after Tom Oberheim’s SEM, swept from low-pass through a notch to high-pass, with envelope curves after the OB-8’s. Oberheim names the OB-X, the Four Voice and the TVS among its ancestors.

timeline.name: Oberheim SEM
timeline.text: The Synthesizer Expander Module: two oscillators and a 12 dB state-variable filter whose mode knob sweeps from low-pass through a notch to high-pass. The TEO-5’s STATE knob is that knob.

timeline.name: Oberheim Two Voice and Four Voice
timeline.text: Two and four SEMs in one case, played from a keyboard: the first Oberheim polysynths, and among the first anywhere.

timeline.name: Oberheim OB-X
timeline.text: Oberheim’s first polysynth built into one case, with patch memory. Oberheim names it as an ancestor of the TEO-5.

timeline.name: Oberheim OB-8
timeline.text: The last of the OB line from the original company. The TEO-5’s envelopes follow its curves.

timeline.name: Sequential Take 5
timeline.text: A five-voice compact poly whose platform and layout the TEO-5 shares: ENV ROUTING, a global LFO 1 and per-voice LFO 2, the mod matrix, overdrive, effects and reverb, the arpeggiator and the sequencer.

timeline.name: Oberheim TEO-5
timeline.text: Five analogue voices on 44 keys: two VCOs with any mix of triangle, sawtooth and pulse, a sub, X-Mod and sync, the SEM-style filter with STATE and a band-pass, two envelopes, two LFOs, a 16-slot mod matrix, VINTAGE, overdrive, one of twelve effects plus a plate reverb, an arpeggiator and a 64-step sequencer.

relatives.name: Sequential Take 5
relatives.text: The same platform and panel layout with a low-pass filter and morphing oscillator shapes in place of the TEO-5’s state-variable filter and wave buttons. This app plays it too.

relatives.name: Oberheim OB-X8
relatives.text: Oberheim’s eight-voice flagship of the same years, also made with Sequential, combining the voices of the OB-X, OB-Xa and OB-8.

relatives.name: Behringer UB-Xa D
relatives.text: A recreation of the OB-Xa, the OB-X’s successor, which this app also plays.

relatives.name: Behringer 2-XM
relatives.text: A recreation of the Two Voice, two SEM-style voices with their multimode filters, which this app also plays.

note: None of the databank’s records name the TEO-5 yet.
